description:
“We are right to be concerned.”

Although the police were “very brave” for dealing with the Golders Green suspect, it is important to keep their actions under scrutiny as they hold “huge powers”, says Green life peer Baroness Jenny Jones. 

Dr Peter Prinsley, Mims Davies, and Baroness Jenny Jones were speaking to Carole Walker (in for Ayesha Hazarika) on Times Radio Drive. Listen live every Saturday and Sunday from 4-7pm.

“He wasn’t dead at all.”

The overwhelming of morgues in Ukraine is causing mistakes in identification, leading to one mother mistakenly being told her son was dead, only to later find out he was alive, says The Sunday Times’s chief foreign correspondent, Christina Lamb.  

Christina Lamb was speaking to Rosie Wright and Calum Macdonald on Times Radio Breakfast. Listen live every day from 6-10am.

author: Times News
description:
At his peak, Carl Hayman was widely regarded as the best tighthead prop in the world. Then, in 2021, at just 41, he was diagnosed with early-onset dementia and probable CTE, a disease linked to the sport he loves, and one that has torn his life apart. In this intimate and devastating interview, David Walsh investigates what happened to Carl, what he’s doing for the players who come after him, and the implications of concussions for rugby’s future. 

#rugby #carlhayman #cte #dementia

The final part of a two-part special investigation into the crisis facing this global game. You can listen to part one here.

Guest: Carl Hayman, retired tighthead prop
